head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:124 — The opt-in gate only exists as a refusal inside `complete()`. The chain resolver still plans `google:gemini-headless`, and every stock Google chain ends in that hop (model-config.yaml:216-309). When an earlier API hop fails for a walkable reason (rate limit, unavailable, retries exhausted), the walk reaches agy. `AgyOptInRequiredError` is a non-retryable `ChevalError`, so the generic arm at head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2544 aborts the whole call with INVALID_CONFIG (exit 2) and replaces the real retryable failure. With the default now off, a host that has `agy` installed loses its working last-resort hop and gets a hard config error. That contradicts the PR's claim that the hop is "not planned" and "never a failed voice". The gated hop should be dropped when the chain is resolved, or treated as a walkable skip, and a test should cover a chain walk that reaches the gated terminal (test_agy_opt_in_gate.py only exercises the adapter on its own).
head/.claude/scripts/flatline-orchestrator.sh:529 — `_tertiary_routes_to_agy` (and `isAgyRouted` at head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:180) count a Google voice as agy-routed only when it is the `gemini-headless` id or the mode is `cli-only`. They ignore `prefer-cli`, and they ignore a Google API model whose catalog `fallback_chain` ends in `gemini-headless`. The planners therefore keep planning voices that cheval will refuse mid-call (see the finding above), so these still show up as failed or DEGRADED voices instead of `disabled_by_opt_in` / `notPlanned`.
head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:494 — `effective_input_ceiling` / `probed_ceiling` are raised 180000 → 936000 by hand. The probe's own outcome was `partial` (budget cap). The accept/reject bracket (972,887 accepted vs ~1,065,182 rejected) is ~92K wide, far outside the 16K tolerance, and the size rejection came from the CLI's own pre-flight check, not from the provider. The value is then recorded as `source: operator_set` with full probe provenance. The new tool's rule is "write the catalog only on a clean outcome" (docs line 296), and this edit bypasses it. The measurement also came through claude-headless on Bedrock, but it is written into the direct-API `auth_type: http_api` entry with `account_limits.tier: unverified`. That raises cheval's preemption threshold 5× for every downstream mount's API route on no API-route evidence, while the entry's own `reprobe_trigger` admits the API probe is still owed. The cited record (grimoires/loa/reports/2026-10-07-opus-5-5-ceiling-probe-cli.json) is not part of the change, so the number cannot be checked.
head/docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md:303 — The migration note presents 936,000 as "measured" and "accepted and verified". It does not say that the probe outcome was partial and the catalog value was set by hand, which the catalog comment (model-config.yaml:496-497) states plainly. Downstream operators are told they inherit a probed bound.
head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:146 — For any entry with `operator_set`/`empirical_probe` + `calibrated_at`, the expected ceiling becomes `min(entry["effective_input_ceiling"], …)`, which is the value under test. The same circularity is at :168 and :299. Apart from the I2 check, the floor tests now accept any hand-edited number once the provenance fields are filled in, which is exactly how the 936000 above got in.
head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:120 — cheval decides the opt-in from the cwd-walk project root. The shell planners read `$CONFIG_FILE`, which adversarial-review.sh:52 lets the environment override, and loa-status has a bats seam. When the two point at different configs, planners and dispatch disagree: a voice is planned that cheval then refuses with INVALID_CONFIG, or the reverse. The shell readers also use mikefarah-only `yq eval … tag == "!!bool"`, so on a python-yq host an operator who opted in has the voice silently dropped by Flatline, the dissent and /loa, while cheval dispatches it (run-preflight.sh is the only reader that handles both yq flavours).
head/.claude/scripts/run-preflight.sh:204 — When a stage's only voice is a gated agy hop, P3 FAILs with "no credential present and no CLI hop on PATH", even though agy may be on PATH and the real cause is the opt-in. The FAIL detail and remediation should name `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in`, not credentials or PATH.
head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/multi-model-pipeline.ts:212 — When every configured voice is `notPlanned` (all agy-routed, opt-in off), the pipeline throws "No models available … (all API keys missing)". That points at API keys when the actual reason is opt_in_required.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

I wrote the review to `/workspace/review.md`. The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**, with 8 findings. I found these by reading the code; I didn't run any of the test suites.

**Blocking issues:**

1. **The agy gate makes cheval fail outright partway through a fallback chain** (`agy_headless_adapter.py:124`, `cheval.py:2544`). The opt-in is enforced only as an error thrown when the agy hop is called. The hop is still in every stock Google fallback chain (the list of models cheval tries in turn), as the last step. If earlier hops fail for a reason that would normally move on to the next one, such as a rate limit, cheval reaches agy and aborts the whole call as a config error (exit 2). That hides the real, retryable failure. It contradicts the PR's claim that the hop is "not planned, never a failed voice". No test covers a chain that reaches the gated hop.
2. **The tools that plan which models to use spot agy routing in only some cases** (`flatline-orchestrator.sh:529`, Bridgebuilder `config.ts:180`). They catch the `gemini-headless` id and `cli-only` mode. They miss `prefer-cli` mode and Google API models whose fallback chain ends in agy. Those voices get planned and then refused by cheval.
3. **The Opus 5.5 input ceiling was raised from 180,000 to 936,000 by hand** (`model-config.yaml:494`). The probe stopped early at its budget cap, and the size where accepted inputs meet rejected ones was narrowed only to about 92K against a 16K tolerance. The new tool itself refuses to write the catalog on an outcome like that. The measurement was also taken through the headless CLI on Bedrock, but it is written into the direct-API entry. The report it cites isn't included in the PR.

**Lesser findings:**

- **Migration doc (`:303`):** it calls 936,000 "measured" and leaves out that the value was set by hand.
- **Catalog floor tests:** for a calibrated entry they compare the ceiling against itself, so they would accept any hand-edited number.
- **Config mismatch:** cheval looks up the opt-in setting from the project root it finds from the current directory. The shell scripts read `$CONFIG_FILE`, which can be overridden. They also use yq syntax that only the Go version of yq understands, so on a host with the Python yq an operator who opted in has agy silently dropped by the scripts while cheval still dispatches it.
- **Misleading errors:** the run preflight check reports "no CLI hop on PATH" when the real cause is the opt-in. Bridgebuilder says "all API keys missing" when every voice was skipped because of the opt-in.
